args: In hunspell/src/hunspell/hashmgr.cxx, assess the safest minimal root-cause fix for the double-free where an AF alias contains ONLYUPCASEFLAG and free_flag treats that shared alias as owned. Are AF flag values expected to permit ONLYUPCASEFLAG, and are there any other ownership paths or internal reserved flags that must be considered? Compare rejecting ONLYUPCASEFLAG in parse_aliasf versus pointer-identity ownership checks in free_flag and direct delete[] sites in add_word.

The sanitizer report shows parse_aliasf allocates aliasf[0], load_tables/get_aliasf stores that shared pointer in an hentry, free_table invokes free_flag, and free_flag deletes it because TESTAFF finds ONLYUPCASEFLAG despite aliasf being nonempty. The destructor then deletes aliasf[0] again. I observed that add_word at hunspell/src/hunspell/hashmgr.cxx lines 368-369 and 388-389 also directly delete vectors inferred as hidden-only-upcase by flag contents, while add_hidden_capitalized_word creates a separately allocated vector with ONLYUPCASEFLAG. The proposed minimal strategy is to reject AF aliases containing the internal ONLYUPCASEFLAG immediately in parse_aliasf after decoding/sorting, clean up current and prior alias allocations, and return false, thereby ensuring no attacker-created shared alias can impersonate an internally owned hidden-capitalization vector.
